reason: Checked against Nicholson himself, because dar-al-masnavi.org carries two Nicholson wordings and one fetch of that page had them reversed. The printed Nicholson translation of Books I and II (Gibb Memorial, 1926; retyped scan, Proem, verse 1) reads “Listen to the reed how it tells a tale, complaining of separations—”. The other wording, “Listen to this reed how it complains: it is telling a tale of separations”, is Nicholson’s LATER correction (1937 commentary volume, after the Konya manuscript reversed hikāyat and shikāyat), so the verifier’s wording is the 1926 text as cited. The only change is a trailing dash (line runs on into verse 2) rendered as a full stop at the cut: standard truncation, no minted words. Locator Book I, line 1 right; Rumi not banned, not at cap, nothing shipped; Poetry is the form. Source 65 chars, no dash. Optional note if the editor wants it: Nicholson later revised the line after the oldest manuscript.
